title: Meanwhile Back In Amsterdam: The Fiftieth Anniversary Of The Bulldog, The First “CoffeeShop”

content_html_sanitized:
Reporting from Amsterdam:

In the early 1970s the Dutch decided that they didn’t like arresting people for possession of cannabis. (Mostly hashish) But where would people buy it? In the rest of the world it would come from the same black market retailers who also sold everything else that is illegal.

 

What the Dutch called the “Separation of the Markets” was fundamental to their drug policy. Prohibition is the real “gateway” between cannabis and “hard drugs”, but recognizing that obvious fact would imply that Prohibition was actually counter productive. Heresy!!

 

Twenty five years ago it was painfully obvious.

From 2000.

The Failure of U.S. Drug Policy What a Prominent Dutch Anti-Prohibitionist Thinks His Prime Minister Should Say To Clinton.

And

Here, if you want cannabis you go to a coffee shop. In other countries if you want it you have to ngo to a man who might try to sell you heroin or cocaine as well."

 

Consequently, lying about The Netherlands, America’s oldest ally, had become an essential part of American marijuana policy. In 1992, when I became the National Director of NORML, I decided that I had to go to Amsterdam. (My work ethic)

See How G. Gordon Liddy, A Watergate Burglar, Inadvertently Helped Fight Marijuana Prohibition

 

One of my most memorable meetings on that trip was with the head of the Amsterdam police “Vice Squad”. He told me that they rarely had to go to a coffeeshop, but problems at bars were routine. (By the way, there are coffeeshops in almost every city and town in The Netherlands. Not just in Amsterdam.)

 

As noted, in the 1970s most of the cannabis was hashish smuggled from places that may also produce opium, but by the 1990s Dutch (and American expats) were growing (still illegal) Nederwiet and Nederhash, which displaced a large part of the smuggled cannabis. (Something similar was happening in Canada.)

See When I Say That Marijuana Prohibition Causes Long Term Memory Loss, The Story of “BC Bud” Is The Best Evidence.

 

So how did it all turn out?

See Dutch youth continues to rank among the healthiest and happiest in Europe - News

May 19,  2020 — Dutch youths also reported considerably less psychosomatic disorders (such as headaches and unhappiness) than their European age-group peers.

How do Prohibitionists explain this?

They don’t, and they don’t even have to lie about it. They just pretend it doesn’t exist and our “news media” let them.

I will be here for the rest of the week reporting on the cannabis scene, including The Bulldog celebration and some of my favorite places. Work, work, work!
